card.name: Words after hedged or modal phrasing
card.fires_on: Short function words or verbs right after a hedge or modal phrase (might, expected, consider, let no, attitude to), where the sentence is still unfolding.

modes.label: After modal or hedge
modes.description: Verb or linking word following might, should, expected or a stance phrase.
modes.example: Yes, one wonders what the Framers might<< have>> thought of free speech.

modes.label: Inside drug advice phrases
modes.description: A word such as of, use or dis right after consider withdrawal, concomitant or a decision to.
modes.example: Consider withdrawal<< of>> NSAIDs, including diclofenac

modes.label: Open rhetorical question
modes.description: A verb in a question about what people will do or take.
modes.example: What will the unemployed - especially the long-term unemployed with only dim memories of integration into the world of work -<< do>> with themselves and their time?

card.writes: Weakly favors adverbs like largely and mostly and disfavors Chinese words for 'may/possibly'; no coherent effect.
card.plain: It fires on small words that follow a hedge or modal phrase, just before the sentence's main point arrives.
